parent_context.note: Parent sprint used the pre-Enuncia outline format (outline.md) with no experience slices, so every slice here is new. Sprint 5's Equinox HUD is carried forward unchanged in look and behavior (ES-1, ES-4).

experience_slices.title: The game plays with no server running
experience_slices.description: Opening or reloading the game starts a new game, and the Equinox HUD and team selection look and behave exactly as before. Nothing has to be running except the game itself.

experience_slices.title: Saves live on the player's own machine
experience_slices.description: Games can be saved to, loaded from, listed in, and deleted from 10 slots stored locally on the player's machine. Corrupted or older saves are handled as gracefully as today. There is no save UI this sprint (the demo loop fits in one play session); storage is shaped so autosaves alongside manual saves can be added later.

experience_slices.title: Every system that works today still works inside the client
experience_slices.description: Combat, narrative, dialogue, and personality run inside the game itself with identical rules, outcomes, and rejections — including the rules that today live only in the server's routes. These systems have no UI until Sprints 7–8; automated tests are the proof they still work.

experience_slices.title: The game opens onto a scene stage
experience_slices.description: The game window is a rendered scene showing a plain backdrop in the HUD's existing background color, with the HUD layered on top and unchanged. The stage is ready for the Sprint 7 town to be dropped in.

experience_slices.title: The designer starts the game with one command
experience_slices.description: One command starts the game and one command verifies everything. The server code and its packages are gone, and the project's instructions no longer describe a server, port, or REST API.

design_decisions.rationale: Designer decision 2026-10-23. One install, one toolchain, one place for all future code; the Steam wrapper later wraps one app. Supersedes ADR-046's separate client folder (its reason — a backend beside it — is gone) and retires ADR-052.

design_decisions.decision: Engine folders stay in place under src/; React moves to src/ui/
design_decisions.rationale: Zero churn on ~9,600 engine lines and their history; the engine/UI boundary is enforced by tsconfig and lint instead of by folder nesting.

design_decisions.decision: Engine, session, and persistence type-check with no DOM or Node globals
design_decisions.rationale: Keeps the engine portable to the desktop build and a possible console port (ADR-055: the tests become the port's spec).

design_decisions.rationale: The global would need a DOM/Node type and break the engine's no-platform-globals rule; uuid is pure and portable.

design_decisions.decision: Server stays runnable until T12 via an interim tsconfig and kept packages
design_decisions.rationale: T5's tests are ported against live route behavior; T12 deletes the server only after the session and ports are in.

TypeScript 6 changes several defaults (e.g. `types` defaults to [], strict on); set `types`, `strict`, `module`, `moduleResolution`, `target` explicitly in every tsconfig rather than relying on defaults. Vite 8 uses Rolldown: use `build.rolldownOptions` if any bundler option is ever needed (none expected). If Vitest 5 breaks engine tests in a way that is not a quick config fix, pin vitest ^4.1.12 instead and report it. After the merge, run `npm run verify`: all engine tests, all existing client tests (now under src/ui), and the HTTP-driven tests must still pass. Watch .gitignore: `*.js` is ignored except `*.config.js`, which is fine for this TS-only repo.

tasks.title: Game session core
tasks.description: An in-client game session that holds this player's single active game and offers the operations the game and player/NPC routes offer today: start a new game, read the current state, read the player and their personality, adjust personality, set the team, and list/look up NPCs. Rules and error outcomes match today's routes, including the input rules that Fastify's request schemas enforced. Also builds the session's foundation that T3, T4, and T8 extend: the result type, the session state holder with change subscription, content injection, and input validation.
acceptance_criteria: Each operation produces the same resulting game state as the corresponding route does today for the same inputs
Error outcomes match today: no active game, unknown NPC, personality adjustment with no recognized traits, team not exactly two companions, team change during combat or an active narrative scene
Every operation produces a new state; earlier states are never altered
Nothing in the session depends on a server or network
A refused or read-only operation leaves the snapshot reference unchanged and does not notify subscribers; a changing operation notifies exactly once
An unexpected engine error returns INTERNAL_ERROR and leaves the game unchanged
Starting a new game clears any pending combat orders and last fight result
tasks.technical_approach: New module src/session/ (pure TypeScript, engine tsconfig: no DOM/Node globals). (1) Result model — src/session/result.ts: `SessionResult<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: SessionError }`, `SessionError = { code: ErrorCode; message: string; details?: unknown; cause?: unknown }`, helpers ok(data), fail(code, message, details?), and fromThrown(err): an Error carrying a `.code` that is a known ErrorCode becomes fail(code, err.message); anything else becomes fail('INTERNAL_ERROR', 'An unexpected error occurred', undefined, err) — mirroring today's globalErrorHandler 500 fallback. Refusals are values, never thrown. (2) Session state — src/session/sessionState.ts: `SessionState = { game: GameState | null; pendingDeclarations: readonly CombatAction[]; lastCombatOutcome: CombatOutcome | null }` (CombatOutcome = { status: 'victory' | 'defeat'; round: number }, used by T4), `initialSessionState`, and `startFresh(game)` which returns a SessionState with the given game, pendingDeclarations [] and lastCombatOutcome null (used by newGame and, in T8, load). (3) Operations — pure functions in src/session/operations/<area>.ts, one file per old route file, signature `(s: SessionState, content: SessionContent, ...inputs) => Outcome<T>` where `Outcome<T> = { next: SessionState; result: SessionResult<T> }`. A refusal or a read returns `next === s` (same reference). This task: operations/game.ts (newGame, getState), operations/player.ts (getPlayer, getPersonality, adjustPersonality, setTeam), operations/npc.ts (listNpcs, getNpc). (4) Holder — src/session/gameSession.ts: `createGameSession(options?: { content?: Partial<SessionContent>; saves?: SaveStore })` returns a `GameSession` object whose methods call the operations, commit `next` when it differs from the current snapshot, and notify listeners. Exposes `getSnapshot(): SessionState` (stable reference between changes) and `subscribe(listener): () => void` — the shape React's useSyncExternalStore expects (T6). The `saves` option is accepted but unused until T8. (5) Content — src/session/content.ts: `SessionContent = { sceneGraph; encounters: Record<string, EncounterConfig>; dialogues: Record<string, DialogueNode[]> }` and `defaultContent` (sceneGraph and encounters filled by T3/T4; start with empty records typed correctly). createGameSession merges options.content over defaultContent so tests and future content can swap pieces. (6) Input validation — src/session/validation.ts: explicit checks that replace the Fastify JSON schemas, each returning a VALIDATION_ERROR SessionError or null. For this task: personality adjustment must be a plain object with at least one key, every key one of the six traits, every value a finite number (no unknown keys — matches `additionalProperties: false, minProperties: 1`); team must be an array of exactly two strings, each at most 64 chars. Order of checks mirrors today: input validation first (schemas ran before handlers), then GAME_NOT_FOUND, then rules. (7) Ported route rules: newGame ignores options and calls createNewGameState(), then startFresh (fix: clears pending combat orders and last fight result — designer decision); getState → GAME_NOT_FOUND 'No active game' when none; getPlayer/getPersonality → GAME_NOT_FOUND when none; adjustPersonality → applyPersonalityAdjustment, returns the new GameState; setTeam → combatState !== null ⇒ TEAM_COMPOSITION_INVALID 'Cannot change team during combat'; narrativeState !== null ⇒ TEAM_COMPOSITION_INVALID 'Cannot change team during narrative scene'; else updateTeamComposition (its own TEAM_COMPOSITION_INVALID throws map via fromThrown) and return { team }; listNpcs → getAllNPCs() templates (no game required); getNpc(id) → live state.npcs[id] when a game is active, else template getNPC(id), else NPC_NOT_FOUND `NPC not found: "${id}"` (ADR-042). Add `INTERNAL_ERROR` to ErrorCodes in src/types/index.ts. Barrel src/session/index.ts exports createGameSession, GameSession, SessionState, SessionResult, SessionError, SessionContent, defaultContent.
tasks.interfaces: Receives: engine functions createNewGameState (src/state/gameState.ts), applyPersonalityAdjustment and updateTeamComposition (src/state/stateUpdaters.ts), getAllNPCs and getNPC (src/state/npcs.ts), ErrorCodes and types (src/types). Produces: `GameSession` (methods newGame(), getState(), getPlayer(), getPersonality(), adjustPersonality(adj), setTeam(npcIds), listNpcs(), getNpc(id), getSnapshot(), subscribe(fn)) returning SessionResult<T>; the operation-module pattern, Outcome<T>, startFresh, validation helpers, and SessionContent that T3/T4/T8 extend. Consumed by T6 (provider), T5/T7 (tests), T8 (save operations attach to the same holder).

design_decisions.decision: Operations return a success-or-refusal result instead of throwing
design_decisions.rationale: Refusals are ordinary gameplay outcomes the UI must show; mirrors today's ApiResponse so the T5 port is mechanical; precedent ADR-033 (discriminated-union result).

design_decisions.decision: Session is one mutable slot holding immutable snapshots, with subscribe/getSnapshot
design_decisions.rationale: Same 'mutable location, immutable contents' principle as ADR-022 without Fastify; snapshot identity changes exactly when state changes, which React's useSyncExternalStore needs (T6).

design_decisions.decision: Pending combat orders and the last fight result live in session state, not GameState
design_decisions.rationale: They were route-plugin memory before (not saved); keeping them out of GameState leaves the save format unchanged.

design_decisions.rationale: Brief: rules and error outcomes match today, including ones that lived only in the server layer.

design_decisions.rationale: Tests swap in fixtures; Sprint 7 adds town content the same way.

tasks.producer_notes: Source of truth for every rule and message: src/api/game.ts, src/api/player.ts, src/api/npc.ts, and src/api/index.ts (globalErrorHandler) — read them before writing each operation and keep messages identical. Operations must never mutate: build new SessionState objects with spread; return the same `s` reference for reads and refusals so the holder does not notify. Wrap every engine call in try/catch → fromThrown so an engine throw can never escape a GameSession method. Do not import anything from src/api (it is deleted in T12). No console, window, or Node APIs (engine tsconfig forbids them). Follow the engine's `.js` import specifier style. getSnapshot must return the same object until a commit happens. Implement GameSession as a plain object of closures (not a class relying on this), so methods such as subscribe and getSnapshot can be passed unbound — T6 hands them straight to useSyncExternalStore.

tasks.title: Narrative and dialogue in the session
tasks.description: Add the narrative and dialogue operations to the game session: start a scene, get the current scene (with personality gating), make a choice, read narrative state, reset narrative, read team synergy, start a dialogue with an NPC, and choose a dialogue option. Narrative matches today's routes except that starting a scene that does not exist is refused. Dialogue is fixed to work as the engine intended: the session owns each NPC's conversation, tracks the player's position in it on the game state, and returns real nodes — with a one-line placeholder greeting for Elena, Lars, and Kade until Sprint 7 writes their dialogue.
acceptance_criteria: Making a narrative choice applies that choice's consequence before advancing the scene, exactly as today
Team synergy is calculated from the player's personality against all NPC personalities, as today
Error outcomes match today: no active game, no active narrative, unknown scene or choice, unknown NPC
Starting a scene that is not in the scene graph is refused with SCENE_NOT_FOUND and the game is unchanged

Starting a dialogue with Elena, Lars, or Kade returns their placeholder greeting node (id `<npcId>_greet`) with only the options the player's personality unlocks, and records it as the current dialogue node

Choosing a dialogue option uses the session's own tree, applies the same personality/NPC/log changes as today's engine, and moves the current dialogue node to the next node (or clears it when the conversation ends)
Choosing with no active conversation is refused with DIALOGUE_NOT_ACTIVE; unknown option, unavailable (gated) option, and missing node keep today's codes
tasks.technical_approach: operations/narrative.ts — port of src/api/narrative.ts using content.sceneGraph (defaultContent.sceneGraph = TEST_SCENE_GRAPH from src/narrative/fixtures.ts, exactly what the route uses today). startScene(sceneId): validate string ≤128 chars (VALIDATION_ERROR) → GAME_NOT_FOUND → NEW: scene id not in the scene graph ⇒ SCENE_NOT_FOUND `Scene "${id}" not found in scene graph` → initializeNarrative; returns narrativeState. getCurrentScene(): GAME_NOT_FOUND → NARRATIVE_NOT_STARTED 'Narrative has not been started' → getCurrentScene(narrativeState, personality, sceneGraph), null ⇒ SCENE_NOT_FOUND. makeChoice(choiceId): validate string ≤128 → GAME_NOT_FOUND → advanceNarrative(state, choiceId, sceneGraph); an error result maps to its code; on success look up the current scene and chosen choice, apply applyConsequence when the choice has one, THEN updateNarrativeState (consequence before advancing, exactly as today); returns { narrativeState, nextScene }. getNarrativeState() → { narrativeState } (may be null). resetNarrative() → clearNarrative, returns { narrativeState: null }. getSynergy() → calculateSynergy(player personality, personalities of Object.values(state.npcs) with a truthy personality — live NPC state, DEFAULT_PARADIGMS). operations/dialogue.ts — NEW behavior (designer decision 'fix everything'). Content: defaultContent.dialogues maps npcId → DialogueNode[] loaded from src/fixtures/dialogues/placeholders.json (import with `with { type: 'json' }`, same pattern as encounter.json). Placeholder content: for each of npc_scout_elena, npc_merchant_lars, npc_outlaw_kade one node `${npcId}_greet` (npcId set, text a single neutral line such as '<Name> nods in greeting.') with one ungated option { id: 'opt_farewell', text: 'Farewell.', nextNodeId: null }. Mark the file clearly as placeholder content for Sprint 7 to replace. The session builds a nodeId → { npcId, tree } index from content.dialogues at creation. startDialogue(npcId): GAME_NOT_FOUND → template getNPC(npcId) missing ⇒ NPC_NOT_FOUND (matches today) → tree missing or no `${npcId}_greet` node ⇒ DIALOGUE_NODE_NOT_FOUND (via engine getStartingNode) → set game.currentDialogueNode to the start node id (new state) → return { node, availableOptions: getAvailableOptions(node, personality) }. chooseDialogueOption(optionId): validate string → GAME_NOT_FOUND → currentDialogueNode null ⇒ DIALOGUE_NOT_ACTIVE (new code) → node id not in the index ⇒ DIALOGUE_NODE_NOT_FOUND → option not on node ⇒ DIALOGUE_OPTION_NOT_FOUND → gate not met ⇒ DIALOGUE_OPTION_NOT_AVAILABLE (checked by the session with engine helpers, so no message-text matching is needed) → processDialogueSelection(state, npcId, nodeId, optionId, tree) → set currentDialogueNode to nextNode?.id ?? null → return { state, nextNode, availableOptions (for nextNode, [] when ended), selectedOptionId }. Add engine updater `setCurrentDialogueNode(state, nodeId | null)` to src/state/stateUpdaters.ts following the updater pattern (spread + updateTimestamp). Add `DIALOGUE_NOT_ACTIVE` to ErrorCodes. Because currentDialogueNode is already part of GameState and save validation, a save taken mid-conversation resumes at the same node (verified in T8/T9). Wire all eight methods onto GameSession.
tasks.interfaces: Receives: T2's SessionState/Outcome/result/validation/content pattern; engine initializeNarrative, updateNarrativeState, clearNarrative (stateUpdaters), getCurrentScene (narrative/sceneEngine), advanceNarrative (narrative/narrativeStateMachine), applyConsequence (narrative/choiceEngine), calculateSynergy (narrative/synergyCalculator), DEFAULT_PARADIGMS (fixtures/synergyConfig), getStartingNode, findNode, getAvailableOptions, evaluatePersonalityGate, processDialogueSelection (dialogue/dialogueEngine), getNPC (state/npcs). tasks.title: Combat in the session
tasks.description: Add the combat operations to the game session: start an encounter from the available encounter configurations, declare player actions, advance a round, and read combat visual state, round history, and result. Matches today's routes, with the fixes the designer approved: a fully refused declaration changes nothing, starting a fight while one is running is refused, and the last fight's result stays readable after it ends.
acceptance_criteria: Declaring actions validates each one; a rejected action with a fallback (e.g., group action falling back to attack) is replaced by its fallback; a new declaration replaces the previous one; a declaration where every action is rejected is refused and leaves the previous declaration in place
Advancing a round resolves it with the pending declarations, clears them, syncs the result into the game, and ends combat on victory or defeat

tasks.technical_approach: Rewrite src/persistence/ as a platform-neutral module (engine tsconfig: no DOM/Node globals). Layer 1 — backends (src/persistence/backends.ts): `SaveBackend = { read(key): Promise<string | null>; write(key, value): Promise<void>; remove(key): Promise<void> }`; `createMemoryBackend()` (Map-based, for tests and as the session's default); `createWebStorageBackend(storage: StorageLike)` where `StorageLike = { getItem(k): string | null; setItem(k, v): void; removeItem(k): void }` is declared locally (no DOM types) and the real window.localStorage is passed in by the app. A write that throws (QuotaExceededError or any storage failure) is rethrown as a coded Error STORAGE_ERROR 'Not enough storage space to save' (quota) or 'Save storage is unavailable' (other). Layer 2 — format (src/persistence/saveFormat.ts): envelope `{ format: 'ancient-order-save', version: 1, kind: 'manual', slot, savedAt: number, playerName: string, game: GameState }`; key scheme `ancient-order/saves/<kind>/<slot>` (only kind 'manual', slots 1-10, this sprint; 'auto' reserved); `parseSave(raw)` → envelope or a corrupted reason (invalid JSON, wrong format tag, unsupported version, invalid game); `normalizeOlderSave(game)` applies today's defaults — missing narrativeState → null, missing team → [], missing reactionProgress → {} — after validation, exactly as loadGame does today; version gate leaves room for future migrations. Layer 3 — validation (src/persistence/validation.ts): move validateGameState and ValidationResult verbatim from src/persistence/saveLoad.ts (all seven phases, personality range 5-35 and sum 100 ± 0.01). Layer 4 — store (src/persistence/saveStore.ts): `createSaveStore(backend): SaveStore` with async `save(slot, game): Promise<SaveMetadata>`, `load(slot): Promise<GameState>`, `list(): Promise<SaveSlotInfo[]>`, `remove(slot): Promise<void>`; slots MIN_SLOT 1 / MAX_SLOT 10; it throws coded Errors following the engine convention (INVALID_SLOT, SAVE_NOT_FOUND, VALIDATION_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR) which the session maps with fromThrown. `SaveMetadata = { slot, timestamp, playerName }` (timestamp = the envelope's savedAt, so save and list agree — fix). `SaveSlotInfo = { slot, exists: boolean, status: 'empty' | 'saved' | 'corrupted', metadata?: SaveMetadata }` — exists stays true only for loadable saves (today's meaning); status distinguishes damaged slots (fix). save validates the game first and refuses invalid state with VALIDATION_ERROR (fix). load: missing → SAVE_NOT_FOUND; invalid JSON or envelope or game → VALIDATION_ERROR `Save file in slot N is corrupted: <reasons>` (fix for invalid JSON, per ADR-043). Barrel src/persistence/index.ts. Session wiring (src/session/operations/saves.ts, async): saveToSlot(slot), loadFromSlot(slot), listSlots(), deleteSlot(slot). Order: slot rule first (integer 1-10 else INVALID_SLOT 'Slot must be an integer between 1 and 10' — the route message), then GAME_NOT_FOUND where a game is needed (save only), then the store. saveToSlot returns SaveMetadata; loadFromSlot commits startFresh(loadedGame) — clears pending combat orders and last fight result (designer fix) — and returns the GameState; listSlots returns 10 SaveSlotInfo; deleteSlot returns { slot, deleted: true } and never touches the active game. createGameSession's `saves` option takes a SaveStore; default createSaveStore(createMemoryBackend()). Add STORAGE_ERROR to ErrorCodes. App wiring: in the app's session creation (src/ui/appSession.ts from T6) pass `saves: createSaveStore(createWebStorageBackend(window.localStorage))`; if accessing window.localStorage throws (storage disabled), fall back to the memory backend.

A future desktop build adds a file-based SaveBackend; a future save UI and autosave use these methods and the reserved 'auto' kind.

tasks.title: Scene renderer
tasks.description: Add the game-rendering framework to the client. It starts with the game, runs one empty scene, can be told which scene to show (so Sprint 7 can add the town as a new scene), and shuts down cleanly when the app unmounts or hot-reloads.
acceptance_criteria: The renderer starts when the game opens and shows the empty scene
A new scene can be added and switched to without changing how the renderer is started
Reloading or hot-reloading never leaves a duplicate or orphaned render surface
Phaser is loaded as a separate chunk and is never imported by engine, session, persistence, or UI test code

decisions.rationale: Brief and ADR-055 assign this choice to the design phase with the designer deciding

tasks.technical_approach: Phaser 4 (designer decision 2026-10-23; add dependency phaser ^4.2.1). Framework-neutral contract in src/render/renderer.ts: `StageRenderer = { showScene(key: SceneKey): void; destroy(): void }` and `CreateRenderer = (parent: HTMLElement, options: { backgroundColor: string; initialScene: SceneKey }) => StageRenderer`. Scene keys in src/render/sceneKeys.ts with no Phaser import: `SCENE_KEYS = ['stage'] as const; type SceneKey = (typeof SCENE_KEYS)[number]`. Phaser side, loaded lazily so Phaser is its own chunk and never loads in jsdom tests: src/render/phaserRenderer.ts exports `createPhaserRenderer: CreateRenderer`, which returns a StageRenderer immediately and inside does `import('./phaserGame')`; showScene calls made before the game is ready are queued (last one wins); destroy() before ready sets a flag so the game is never created, destroy() after ready calls game.destroy(true) (removes the canvas). src/render/phaserGame.ts imports Phaser and the registry and builds the Game: type AUTO (WebGL with Canvas fallback), parent, backgroundColor from options, scale { mode: Phaser.Scale.RESIZE } so the canvas tracks the parent's size without stretching, banner false, audio { noAudio: true } until a later sprint adds sound (avoids autoplay warnings), every registry scene added and only initialScene started; showScene(key) stops the other active scenes and starts key. Scene registry src/render/scenes/index.ts: `SCENES: Record<SceneKey, typeof Phaser.Scene> = { stage: StageScene }` — the Record type forces every key to have a scene class, so Sprint 7 adds 'town' to SCENE_KEYS plus one entry here. src/render/scenes/StageScene.ts: a Phaser.Scene with key 'stage' that draws nothing (the camera shows the game background color). React bridge src/ui/components/SceneStage.tsx: props { scene: SceneKey; createRenderer?: CreateRenderer } (default createPhaserRenderer); renders a single div (ref) that fills its container; effect keyed on createRenderer creates the renderer with backgroundColor read from the CSS custom property --color-bg-deep on document.documentElement (fallback '#1a1410') and initialScene = scene, cleanup destroys it — this makes StrictMode double-mount and Fast Refresh safe; a second effect keyed on scene calls renderer.showScene(scene). vite.config.ts: set build.chunkSizeWarningLimit to fit the Phaser chunk (~1.4 MB minified) with a comment explaining why.
tasks.interfaces: Produces: SceneStage React component (consumed by T11's App layout), StageRenderer/CreateRenderer contract (tests pass a fake factory), SceneKey and the scene registry (Sprint 7 adds the town scene, Sprint 8 the combat scene). Receives: the --color-bg-deep design token from src/ui/styles/tokens.css. Does not read game state this sprint.

design_decisions.decision: Rendering framework: Phaser 4 (not PixiJS)
design_decisions.rationale: Designer decision 2026-10-23. Phaser includes tilemaps (Tiled), cameras, input, animation, tweens, audio, loader, and scene management that the Sprint 7 town and Sprint 8 combat need; PixiJS would require assembling and maintaining add-ons for each. Bundle size difference (~360 KB vs ~150 KB gzip, measured) is irrelevant for a desktop download.

design_decisions.decision: Renderer sits behind a small framework-neutral contract and is injected into the React bridge
design_decisions.rationale: Tests use a fake; Phaser stays out of jsdom; the React side never imports Phaser directly.

design_decisions.decision: Phaser loads lazily as its own chunk
design_decisions.rationale: Keeps the HUD's code path light and lets the stage boot after the HUD renders; same backdrop color on body and canvas means no visible flash.

design_decisions.decision: Scale mode RESIZE
design_decisions.rationale: Canvas matches the window exactly with no stretching or letterboxing (T11: fill without distortion).

design_decisions.decision: Audio disabled until a sprint adds sound
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids browser autoplay warnings for a scene with no audio.

tasks.producer_notes: Phaser 4 is recent (4.0 April 2026); prefer the official Phaser 4 docs/API over Phaser 3 examples, which may use renamed or removed APIs. Only src/render/phaserGame.ts and src/render/scenes/** may import 'phaser' (statically); everything else uses the contract and SceneKey. Do not draw anything in StageScene — no art this sprint.

tasks.technical_approach: CSS Modules + existing design tokens (ADR-047). src/ui/App.tsx renders: an app root (position fixed, inset 0, overflow hidden — the page never scrolls) containing `<SceneStage scene="stage" createRenderer={createRenderer} />` in a stage layer (position absolute, inset 0, z-index 0) and a HUD layer above it (position absolute, inset 0, z-index 1) that takes over today's .app layout exactly — display flex, justify-content center, align-items flex-start, padding var(--space-lg) — so the HUD sits where it does today.
